commands.wildfires.tfctime.set: TFC calendar speed set to %sx (equivalent day length: %s minutes); server remains at 20 TPS
commands.wildfires.tfctime.cleared: TFC calendar acceleration cleared: %sx (%s-minute day); server remains at 20 TPS
commands.wildfires.tfctime.query: Current TFC calendar speed: %sx (equivalent day length: %s minutes); server TPS is unchanged
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.started: Accelerating the entire TFC calendar at %2$sx until %1$s; local observer: %3$s, %4$s, %5$s. Speed returns to 1x when the event begins
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.waiting: %s is already active; waiting for it to end before tracking the next natural occurrence
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.rainbow: A rainbow also requires a real rain transition. This command does not change weather, so the wait depends on natural rainfall
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.none: No TFC-time event is currently being tracked
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.reached: %s began naturally at TFC calendar tick %s; calendar speed automatically returned to 1x
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.overwor: Local sky events can only be tracked in the Overworld
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.aurora_: This position is below 50 degrees absolute latitude, so the default aurora rule can never trigger; move to a polar region first
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.observe: Event acceleration was cancelled and restored to 1x because the initiator disconnected or left the Overworld
commands.wildfires.tfctime.until.time_ju: Event acceleration was cancelled and restored to 1x after an external calendar jump
